newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan refinery slowdown shuts one topping unit.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan refinery slowdown shuts one topping unit.

text.p: Taiwan's state-owned Chinese Petroleum said on Monday a major operational slowdown at its Taoyuan refinery included the total shutdown of one of two topping units.

"Chinese Petroleum has shut down Taoyuan's No.1 topping unit to cut costs and waiting for the Control Yuan's inspection for safety concerns," said a manager at Chinese Petroleum's Taoyuan facility, the monopoly firm's only north Taiwan refinery.
The manager said the Control Yuan, the central government's top investigative body, has ordered a safety examination into an August 13 oil-pump fire unrelated to Monday's shutdown.
Chinese Petroleum on Monday slashed the refinery's output to just 34 percent of capacity as a pipeline problem shut down its offshore crude offloading facility, halting its crude supply.
The reduction in output aimed to allow the refinery to maintain operations with the limited supplies of crude on hand, managers said.
The company confirmed early on Monday that it had shut down both of its offshore crude-offloading systems late last week due to unspecified pipeline problems.
Chinese Petroleum officials told Reuters the refinery had about 407,000 kilolitres crude supplies on hand, enough to keep the refinery running at full speed for only about 10 days.

The refinery manager said engineers would feed about 12,000 kilolitres or 70,000 barrels of crude a day into the facility, effective immediately, just 34 percent of its full capacity consumption of 35,000 kilolitres or 200,000 barrels.
Officials declined to say whether the decision to slow down the refinery's operation indicated a possibility that repairs to the pipeline could take longer than 10 days.
Chinese Petroleum spokesman Fang Yi-shan had told Reuters earlier on Monday that repairs were not expected to take longer than 10 days.
